primary.title: Memoirs of Catherine the Great
primary.author: Catherine II of Russia
primary.rationale: Catherine's personal memoirs offer direct insight into her thoughts, experiences, and perspectives during her rise to power and reign. These are foundational primary sources for understanding her.

primary.title: The Correspondence of Catherine the Great
primary.author: Catherine II of Russia
primary.rationale: Her extensive correspondence with prominent figures of her time (e.g., Voltaire, Diderot, Frederick the Great) reveals her intellectual engagement, political strategies, and personal opinions on a wide range of topics.

primary.title: Nakaz (Instruction) of Catherine the Great
primary.author: Catherine II of Russia
primary.rationale: This document outlines Catherine's legislative program and her vision for Russia, heavily influenced by Enlightenment ideas. It is a key primary source for her reformist agenda.

secondary.title: Catherine the Great: A Short Biography
secondary.author: Isabel de Madariaga
secondary.rationale: Isabel de Madariaga is a leading scholar on Catherine the Great. This work, though a short biography, is based on extensive research and provides a concise yet authoritative overview of her reign.

secondary.title: Catherine the Great: Portrait of a Woman
secondary.author: Robert K. Massie
secondary.rationale: Robert K. Massie is a renowned biographer. This book offers a comprehensive and engaging narrative of Catherine's life and reign, drawing on a wide array of historical sources.

secondary.title: Catherine the Great: The Empress and the Enlightenment
secondary.author: W. Bruce Lincoln
secondary.rationale: W. Bruce Lincoln's work focuses on Catherine's engagement with Enlightenment ideals and their impact on her policies and reign, offering a scholarly analysis of a crucial aspect of her rule.

suggestions.notes: Primary source dates reflect the period of writing or publication, not necessarily the earliest available edition. Secondary sources are chosen for their scholarly reputation and relevance to Catherine's reign and intellectual context.
